title: You, and whatever you worship.
subtitle: The idolaters and their idols addressed together
then: Allah now speaks directly to the idolaters. Ibn Kathir explains the address as {trap}you and those whom you worship{/trap} together. {idea}The sentence is left open here, and the next verse finishes it.{/idea}
now: The influencer and the lifestyle they sell. The crowd and the trend it worships. {trap}Together they look unstoppable.{/trap} {idea}Wait for how Allah finishes the sentence.{/idea}
old: Those who push false things together have a lot of power over me.
new: Whatever people gather around besides Allah, together they still cannot own my heart.
try: Notice one trend you feel pulled by today. Name it, and remind yourself it has no power over your choice.

title: You cannot lure anyone away from Him.
subtitle: False worship has no hold on a turned heart

row.title: Allah
sub: no one tempts away from Him

then: The small band of believers in Makkah was under heavy pressure, and the idolaters seemed to hold every advantage. Allah tells them: {idea}you cannot tempt anyone away from Him.{/idea} {trap}Their mockery and power{/trap} could not reach a heart that belonged to Allah.
now: You worry about your teenager, your new-Muslim friend, yourself. {trap}The world is loud and very persuasive.{/trap} {idea}It is not stronger than Allah's hold on a heart that turns to Him.{/idea}
old: With so much pressure around, keeping faith is a losing battle.
new: No one can pull a heart from Allah if it keeps turning to Him.
try: Make a short dua today asking Allah to keep your heart firm on faith.

title: Only those already heading for the Fire follow them.
subtitle: Who false worship actually reaches

key.label: What makes someone open to it

then: Ibn Kathir explains that the only ones who follow such false worship are {trap}those more misguided than its callers.{/trap} He links them to the verse about people who {idea}have hearts they do not understand with, eyes they do not see with, and ears they do not hear with.{/idea}
now: What makes you easy to pull is not how clever the pull is. {trap}It is how heedless you are when it comes.{/trap} The tired, distracted, half-awake heart. {idea}Keep your heart awake and the pull loses its grip.{/idea}
old: People fall for falsehood because it is so convincing.
new: Falsehood wins most easily over a heart that has stopped paying attention.
try: Take two minutes today with your phone away, and simply pay attention to your heart.

title: Every angel has a known place.
subtitle: The angels speak about themselves
then: Against the claim that angels are Allah's daughters, the angels speak. Ibn Kathir says {idea}each has his own place in the heavens which he does not overstep.{/idea} He quotes the Prophet ﷺ: {reward}there is no place in the lowest heaven without an angel standing or prostrating in it.{/reward}
now: You keep comparing your place to everyone else's. Their job, their house, their marriage. {idea}The angels know their place and fill it with worship.{/idea} Your place today is where Allah put you. Fill it well.
old: I would worship better if I were in a different situation.
new: Like the angels, I can serve Allah fully in exactly the place He has given me.
try: Do your main task today with full attention, as worship, right where you are.

title: We are the ones who stand in rows.
subtitle: The angels' rows, and ours in prayer
then: The surah opened by swearing by those ranged in rows. Ibn Kathir reports that Umar would turn to the people before prayer and say: {idea}make your rows straight, for Allah wants you to follow the ways of the angels.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}our rows have been made like the rows of the angels.{/reward}
now: Friday prayer. You are on your phone until the last second, then drift into a gap with half a step between you and the next person. {idea}Your row mirrors the angels' rows.{/idea} Close the gap, stand straight, and mean it.
old: How the rows look in prayer is just a detail.
new: Standing in a straight row, I am joining something the angels do in the heavens.
try: At your next prayer in congregation, close the gap and straighten your row on purpose.

title: We are the ones who glorify Him.
subtitle: Servants, not partners
then: Ibn Kathir explains the angels' words: {idea}we stand in rows and glorify the Lord{/idea}, declaring Him above any fault. {reward}We are His servants and in need of Him, humbling ourselves before Him.{/reward} The beings the idolaters worshipped are themselves worshippers.
now: You put someone on a pedestal: a scholar, a parent, a public figure. {idea}The best of creation glorify Allah and call themselves His servants.{/idea} Respect people, but keep worship for the One they worship.
old: Some people are so holy they are almost beyond being servants.
new: Even the angels say: we are servants who glorify Him. So is everyone I admire.
try: Say Subhan Allah thirty-three times after one prayer today.

title: They used to say something, before he came.
subtitle: What Quraysh said before the Prophet ﷺ
then: Ibn Kathir explains that before the Prophet ﷺ came, Quraysh {trap}used to wish{/trap} for someone to remind them about Allah. This verse opens the quote. {idea}The next two verses tell us what they said.{/idea}
now: If I ever had time, I would read Quran every day. If I lived near a mosque, I would pray there. {trap}We all have used-to-say sentences.{/trap} {idea}The test is what happens when the chance arrives.{/idea}
old: I would do better if the right conditions came.
new: When the chance I wished for arrives, my answer is what counts, not my old wish.
try: Think of one thing you said you would do if you could. If you now can, start it today.

title: If only we had a reminder like the people of old.
subtitle: They wished for a book of their own
then: Ibn Kathir says Quraysh used to wish for {reward}someone to remind them about Allah and bring them the Book of Allah.{/reward} He links it to the verse where they swore that if a warner came, {trap}they would be more guided than any nation.{/trap}
now: If I had grown up in a practicing family. If I could study with a real scholar. {trap}It always feels like the missing piece is outside you.{/trap} {idea}You have the Quran on your phone right now.{/idea}
old: I would be a better Muslim if I had better guidance around me.
new: The reminder is already in my hands. What I need is to open it.
try: Open the Quran today and read just one page with its meaning.

title: We would have been Allah's sincere servants.
subtitle: The promise they made about themselves
then: Ibn Kathir quotes the verse: they swore that if a warner came {reward}they would be more guided than any nation{/reward}, yet when one came {trap}it increased them only in flight from the truth.{/trap} Their promise about themselves did not survive the test.
now: You say, if I ever got rich, I would give so much. If I ever had kids, I would be so patient. {trap}Then the money comes. The kids come.{/trap} {idea}The person you promised to be is waiting to see if you show up.{/idea}
old: I know the kind of person I would be, given the chance.
new: My promises about my future self mean little until I keep them in the present.
try: Keep one small promise today that you made to yourself or to Allah.

title: Then it came, and they rejected it. They will know.
subtitle: The wish granted, and turned down
then: What they asked for arrived. {trap}They disbelieved in it.{/trap} Ibn Kathir calls the ending {idea}a definite and stern threat{/idea} because of their disbelief in their Lord and their rejection of His Messenger ﷺ.
now: You prayed for a job, and when it came you complained about it. You asked Allah for a sign, and when a reminder came you scrolled past. {idea}Sometimes the answer arrives, and the real test is whether you accept it.{/idea}
old: If Allah gave me what I asked for, I would surely be grateful.
new: When what I asked for arrives, I need to recognize and accept it, not wish for something else.
try: Name one prayer of yours that Allah has already answered. Thank Him for it today.
